reviews.title: Top-graded dynamic XLR mic!
reviews.comment: -Quality and construction built feels high quality -comes with swappable mic cover, whether it's black or red -noise level was excellent -no audio distortion -cardioid mode works perfectly fine -However, you may need an audio interface to connect with 48V Phantom power in order to drive this microphone properly but also convert from digital to analog signal for your computer -In addition, you will need to purchase an Elgato Wave Mic Arm Mk.2 in order to mount your XLR microphone -Yes, you will need to purchase XLR balanced cable in order to connect your XLR microphone -Expensive but you pay for high quality graded XLR which is known as balanced mic -built-in shock mount is already included -3.8" adapter is included to mount your XLR mic

reviews.title: 175 dollars?
reviews.comment: THIS IS A STEAL!! The Yeti Studio is an "SM7b" esque microphone with its look and with how it's been EQ'd out of the box.  This microphone is definitely deeper or "muddier" tone than the SM7b but that can work on some voices but better yet since this is about 90% of the way of a SM7b, it can definitely be EQ'd well. It's built well and is quite heavy giving it a "quality" feeling. Not only that, because of the preamp in this microphone, you can use this with a cheap audio interface (Using it on a Behringer UMC22 and you can get very little preamp noise from your interface due to the preamp in the mic). If you can find it at around 200 dollars or less, it's a steal. 250 dollars, depends on what you're looking for in a microphone. 350 dollars? I recommend not getting it, at that price point you can find better microphones or you're most likely going to get an SM7b.

reviews.title: Professional quality microphone
reviews.comment: By far the best microphone I've used. I primarily use it for gaming and it has not disappointed me. While on the more expensive side, especially when you include the XLR cable and audio mixer, It is a very good-sounding microphone that doesn't take much at all to set up apart from hooking it up.
reviews.author: Jacob

reviews.title: A modern Shure SM7B
reviews.comment: This microphone has been nothing short of fantastic. The sound quality is amazing and it's a decent step up from the microphone I used to have, the Wave 3. I use the Wave XLR as my interface and it sounds great. This microphone is very flexible in terms of tuneability and you can sound like anything you want. You can have a very neutral sound, or you can sound like a professional podcaster. The choice is yours. This microphone has some good weight to it. It really feels like you're using a quality product. You will need to provide your own XLR cable. I use the Elgato XLR cable and it works fine. I highly recommend this microphone if you're looking at a high quality device. The ONLY gripe I have is I wish it had better plosive protection, but just move the mic slightly off to the side and that resolves the issue without sacrificing quality.
reviews.author: Wesley
